mission: Adversarial validation of the discovered closed self-edit loop
method: Live source trace, live unpickle of river_brain.pkl, and a purpose-built correlation script joining memory/shadow_accuracy.jsonl (2,028 rows), memory/self_edit_outcomes.jsonl (179 rows, 103 with a real quality delta), and memory/SELF_EDIT.log by timestamp. No code was modified. Do-not-implement constraint honored throughout.

causal_graph_exact.function: save_reflection() call sites at each terminal branch
causal_graph_exact.output: a structured entry with result/model_used/generated_code fields, appended to memory/reflection_shard.jsonl

causal_graph_exact.note: distinct from reflection_shard.py's own separate GENERATIVE reflection loop, which reads only a signal string + past-reflection embeddings and has zero access to this outcome data -- confirmed by direct source read

causal_graph_exact.output: targets.next_self_edit_focus written to memory/self_model.json, live value confirmed = {'next_self_edit_focus':'coding','reason':'avg_quality=2.37 (threshold=2.5), obs=99027'}

causal_graph_exact.persistence: disk JSON, re-read fresh each SelfModelUpdater cycle (130s interval)
causal_graph_exact.downstream_reader: self_edit_manager.perform_self_edit() via SelfModelUpdater().get_weak_task_type(), but ONLY as a fallback -- see arbitration

causal_graph_exact.note: closes the loop back to step 1

signal_a_riverbrain_empirical.source_data: RiverBrain.model_task_stats (per model x task_type running mean of _score_response_quality(), EMA-windowed past 200 observations per Finding 39) plus RiverBrain.observation_counts
signal_a_riverbrain_empirical.aggregation_method: self_model_updater._compute_task_performance() computes avg_quality_score and sample_count per task type from a recent window of memory/interaction_log.jsonl entries; _compute_targets() then requires obs_counts[task] >= _MIN_OBS_FOR_TARGETING AND sample_count>0 AND avg < _WEAK_QUALITY_THRESHOLD, picks the lowest-scoring qualifying task type
signal_a_riverbrain_empirical.time_window: two different horizons deliberately kept separate by the code's own comment: RiverBrain's obs_counts is an all-time count; avg_quality_score/sample_count is a recent-window read -- a task type needs BOTH real historical volume AND a real recent sample to qualify, precisely to avoid a zero-recent-sample task type winning trivially via a default-0.0 average
signal_a_riverbrain_empirical.task_buckets: coding, self_edit_coding, echo_projects_coding, personal, creative, reasoning, general (7 real buckets, live-unpickled counts confirmed: coding n=99,027 combined across sub-buckets is the dominant real signal by orders of magnitude over reasoning n~248 and creative n~384)
signal_a_riverbrain_empirical.update_frequency: SelfModelUpdater._loop() runs on a fixed 130-second timer, unconditional (per CLAUDE.md's own prior finding, re-confirmed structurally this session, not re-timed live)
signal_a_riverbrain_empirical.target_selection_algorithm: _compute_targets(): priority-ordered rule set (weak+well-observed task types ranked by lowest avg_quality_score; fallback to worst-quality-among-observed; final fallback to 'coding')
signal_a_riverbrain_empirical.persistence: memory/self_model.json, plain JSON, overwritten each cycle -- no historical log of prior targets is kept in this file itself
signal_a_riverbrain_empirical.entry_into_perform_self_edit: only as a FALLBACK, via SelfModelUpdater().get_weak_task_type(), reached only if memory/shadow_self_model.json does not exist or its targets.next_self_edit_focus is falsy

signal_b_shadow.source_data: the most recent text passed to shadow_model.propose_from_reflection(reflection_text) -- itself the output of reflection_shard.py's generative free-association loop (a real MLX-model call on a signal + past-reflection context, NOT the structured self-edit outcome data)
signal_b_shadow.reflection_extraction: propose_from_reflection() is called unconditionally from app/emergent_scheduler.py:723-724 on every real reflection cycle (independent of whether that reflection had anything to do with self-edit performance)
signal_b_shadow.keyword_heuristic: 4 fixed task types (reasoning/coding/creative/personal), 5-6 hand-picked keywords each (e.g. coding: code/program/function/debug/implement/script); counts keyword hits in the reflection text, picks the task type with the most hits
signal_b_shadow.threshold: requires best_count >= 2 keyword hits to fire at all; below that, no proposal is written and the existing shadow file (if any) is left unchanged
signal_b_shadow.persistence: memory/shadow_self_model.json -- shadow_model.propose() merges the CURRENT REAL self_model.json as a baseline, then overwrites just the targets key with the heuristic's pick, plus a shadow_proposed_at timestamp
signal_b_shadow.update_frequency: fires whenever a reflection cycle happens to produce >=2 keyword matches for some task type -- live data shows this is frequent: shadow_accuracy.jsonl (a separate, roughly-hourly comparison log, 2,028 total rows) shows the shadow file's focus changing readings in the majority of recent hourly snapshots
signal_b_shadow.entry_into_perform_self_edit: checked FIRST, explicitly commented 'highest-trust signals' in source -- wins over Signal A whenever shadow_self_model.json has any focus value set at all, regardless of Signal A's own confidence/sample size

arbitration_rule_analysis.rule: if shadow_self_model.json exists and has a truthy targets.next_self_edit_focus, use it; else fall back to self_model.json's RiverBrain-derived target; else default to 'coding'
arbitration_rule_analysis.why_shadow_is_trusted_first: the code's own in-line comment calls shadow 'highest-trust signals' without further justification in the source itself. No evidence was found that 'highest trust' was ever validated against 'highest empirical reliability' -- shadow_model.py's own module docstring instead frames the mechanism as an EXPERIMENTAL, freely-overwritable proposal space specifically so it CAN be wrong without touching production self_model.json, and shadow_model.py's own check_and_correct() function explicitly withholds calling propose() for exactly this reason ('Shadow corrections are advisory-only until the signal is externally validated... no external anchor'). The arbitration rule inside perform_self_edit() appears to contradict shadow_model.py's own stated design intent: the module that produces Signal B explicitly disclaims giving it unvalidated authority, while the consumer (perform_self_edit()) treats it as authoritative by default.
arbitration_rule_analysis.conclusion: 'highest trust' in this codebase's own comment does NOT mean highest empirical reliability -- it appears to mean 'most recently and specifically proposed,' a recency/specificity heuristic mistaken for a confidence ranking.

historical_correlation_table_note: Full table (103 rows) in the accompanying .md report. Built by joining each real self_edit_outcomes.jsonl entry that has a computed quality_score.delta to its nearest-preceding shadow_accuracy.jsonl reading (median lag well under 60 minutes). Key result: the ACTUAL target_task_type field on every one of the 103 real, quality-tracked evaluated outcomes reads 'coding' -- 100%, zero exceptions, across a July 5 - September 2 span. The empirical (self_model.json) signal independently read 'coding' at the matched reading in 74/103 (71.8%) of cases; the shadow signal read 'coding' in only 14/103 (13.6%); neither matched in 15/103 (14.6%, both said something else, e.g. reasoning/creative/general, while the real tracked deploy still targeted coding regardless).

quality_outcome_analysis.interpretation: t=1.65 on n=103 (~102 df) corresponds to roughly p~0.10 two-tailed -- NOT significant at the conventional 0.05 threshold. The mean improvement is not statistically distinguishable from a random walk around a small positive constant, given individual swings (-1.47 to +1.71) that are 5-15x the size of the mean itself. This is directly relevant evidence for the regression-to-the-mean falsification hypothesis: it cannot be ruled out with this data.

mean_delta_by_which_signal_matched_actua.interpretation: Mean deltas are nearly identical across all three groups (0.098 vs 0.118 vs 0.114) -- whether the empirical signal, the shadow signal, or neither correctly anticipated the (always-coding) actual target has NO detectable relationship with the resulting quality outcome. This is additional evidence that the realized quality change is not causally traceable to which targeting signal happened to be 'right' at that moment.

reassessed_426_463_figure.original_framing_rejected: 426/463 = 92% 'deployment success' must not be read as '92% self-improvement' -- it measures passing the F1/F2/F3 safety-and-import gate plus the fitness-gate comparison (candidate AST-complexity score >= production AST-complexity score), which this and the prior investigation both confirm is saturated at a perfect 4/4 ceiling for all 25 currently-retained deploys.
reassessed_426_463_figure.this_sessions_own_independently_computed: Among the 179 real self_edit_outcomes.jsonl entries (a DIFFERENT, narrower population -- only entries that reached outcome-tracking, not all 463 historical attempts), 103 (57.5%) have a real, computed pre/post quality_score.delta; of those, 61 (59.2%) show a positive delta, 42 (40.8%) show a negative delta, 0 show exactly zero, and the mean (+0.103) is not statistically significant at conventional thresholds.
reassessed_426_463_figure.these_two_figures_measure_different_thin: 92% answers 'did the candidate pass the safety/AST-complexity gate.' 59.2%/40.8% answers 'did real subsequent production coding-task quality, averaged over a real window of interactions, go up or down after a deploy.' Neither implies the other.
reassessed_426_463_figure.P_quality_improvement_given_accepted_edi: 61/103 = 0.592 (not conditioned on feedback-informed vs. baseline targeting, since 100% of tracked entries share the same 'coding' target -- this specific conditional split from the mission's Part VIII could not be computed, because the data contains no real variation in actual target to condition on)
reassessed_426_463_figure.P_quality_improvement_given_feedback_inf: CANNOT BE COMPUTED -- all 103 tracked, evaluated outcomes share the identical actual target ('coding'), so there is no real historical contrast between a 'feedback-informed' and a 'baseline' target to compare outcomes across. Stated plainly per the mission's own instruction rather than a forced or invented comparison.

error_correction_analysis.within_cycle_retry_confirmed_real: self_edit_manager.py (~lines 1930-1990) contains a genuine within-cycle retry: on a first sandbox-test failure, it builds a retry_prompt that explicitly includes the real error/exception text, calls echo_query() again for a second candidate, tests THAT in sandbox, and calls river.learn_from_sandbox_outcome(retry_model_name, success=True/False, ...) on the retry's own result -- a real attempt -> failure -> diagnosis(actual error fed back) -> retry -> re-verify loop, confirmed by direct source read.
error_correction_analysis.scope_limitation: this is a SINGLE retry within one self-edit cycle, not indefinite iteration, and it is scoped to sandbox-test failure specifically, not to a later-discovered quality regression (which is only detected 25+ minutes after deploy, well past any retry window).
error_correction_analysis.cross_cycle_streak_mechanism: self_edit_convergence.json's non_convergent_streak (real schema, historically used to retire two prompt families per prior project history) currently reads 0 for all 4 live families despite a same-session live SELF_EDIT.log tail showing several consecutive real failures -- this investigation could not fully resolve whether the reset condition is functioning exactly as designed (any candidate reaching dry_run_staged resets it, even without production deployment) or is quietly inert; flagged as unresolved, not concluded either way.

council_rating_forensics.stale_cursor_mechanism: council_cursor.json reads {'position': 33471, 'updated_utc': '2026-07-26T14:15:33Z'}; interaction_log.jsonl currently holds 11,671 real lines. _poll_and_rate()'s `new_lines = lines[cursor:]` on an 11,671-item list with cursor=33471 returns [] via ordinary Python slice semantics -- no exception, no log line, a silent permanent no-op.
council_rating_forensics.confirmed_real_rotation_event: memory/interaction_log.jsonl.1.gz exists, dated 2026-08-22 -- direct, physical proof that interaction_log.jsonl WAS rotated (gzip+truncate) by app/maintenance/night_cycle.py's log-retention mechanism (100MB cap, per its own _LOG_RETENTION_TARGETS entry) roughly a month after the cursor's own last update.
council_rating_forensics.timeline_tension_stated_honestly: the cursor's own updated_utc (2026-07-26) predates the confirmed Aug 22 rotation by about 4 weeks. If the cursor had kept advancing normally through that period, its position would have kept growing past 33,471 right up to the rotation, at which point (and only then) it would have become invalid relative to the freshly-truncated file. The fact that the cursor's own timestamp stopped moving BEFORE the rotation suggests _poll_and_rate() itself may have stopped executing meaningfully around 2026-07-26 for a separate, not-yet-identified reason, with the Aug 22 rotation then compounding (or simply preserving) an already-stalled state rather than being the sole original cause. This was NOT fully resolved in this pass -- historical watchdog/error logs from that period have themselves already been rotated out by the same log-retention mechanism, so the original triggering event could not be directly recovered.
council_rating_forensics.why_no_liveness_check_detected_it: council_river_blend (the real, existing Liveness Ledger check for this mechanism) is a STATIC, source-anchor check -- it verifies that rate_one_entry()'s source still calls learn_from_council_rating() gated by is_council_trusted(), which it does. It has no functional/data-freshness component (e.g., 'has council_ratings.jsonl grown in the last N days'), so a structurally-intact-but-functionally-starved mechanism reads as PASSING. This is the same class of gap CLAUDE.md's own Finding 28 named once before for a different mechanism (self_edit_apply_to_code): a check that verifies the wiring is correct can still be fooled by an upstream data-starvation problem it was never designed to detect.
council_rating_forensics.would_repair_produce_meaningful_state_ch: yes, plausibly -- is_council_trusted() is confirmed True live, meaning any newly-sampled rating would immediately flow through to a real RiverBrain.learn_from_council_rating() call, per the existing, already-verified blend logic (Finding 67's _blend_council_and_quality, re-confirmed intact by the council_river_blend check passing live today).
council_rating_forensics.downstream_consumer: model_task_stats, the exact same structure Signal A above reads -- meaning repairing this would add a second, independent, human/peer-judgment-informed contribution to the SAME routing-level signal already analyzed in this report, not a new content-level learning channel.
council_rating_forensics.routing_only_or_content: routing only -- this repair would strengthen an existing routing-adaptation signal, never response content, consistent with Hard Rule 6.
council_rating_forensics.likely_measurable_benefit: plausible but unconfirmed -- the blend weight (0.3 council / 0.7 quality_score, per Finding 67) means even a fully-repaired cursor would only modestly shift an already-dominant quality_score-driven signal; a real before/after RiverBrain.model_task_stats comparison (mirroring Finding 44's own method) would be required to confirm any measurable magnitude, not assumed.
council_rating_forensics.minimal_regression_test_proposal: a liveness-ledger-style check computing (current_line_count_of_interaction_log - cursor_position); alert if this value is negative (cursor beyond file end) OR if council_ratings.jsonl's most recent timestamp is more than 48h old while interaction_log.jsonl has grown in the same window -- the second condition specifically catches a stuck-cursor-that-happens-to-still-be-numerically-valid case that the first condition alone would miss.

falsification_evidence: The apparent loop could be explained partly by routing effects alone: Signal A (RiverBrain) IS confirmed to be a real, causally-effective routing mechanism (Finding 39's tag-boost) independent of anything shadow-related -- the loop's most defensible real effect is on WHICH MODEL answers a given task type, not on self-edit target selection specifically producing better code.

The RiverBrain signal selecting 'coding' as the target does not, by itself, demonstrate that targeting 'coding' IMPROVES coding -- 100% of tracked real deploys targeted coding across this entire multi-month history, and the resulting quality deltas (mean +0.10, t=1.65, not significant) are consistent with no reliable improvement at all, only noise around a near-zero baseline.

Shadow's disagreement with the empirical signal in 12/15 recent hourly readings could reflect either genuinely poor inference OR simple staleness/mistimed sampling (a reflection about an unrelated topic happening to contain >=2 coincidental keyword hits) -- this investigation found direct evidence for the LATTER explanation (a pure keyword-count heuristic with no semantic understanding), which is a stronger, more parsimonious explanation than 'shadow is doing bad inference about task performance' -- it is not attempting task-performance inference at all.

Regression-to-the-mean cannot be ruled out for the +0.10 mean delta: t=1.65 on n=103 is below the conventional 95% significance threshold, and the near-identical mean deltas across the empirical/shadow/neither-matched subgroups (0.098/0.118/0.114) show no relationship between which signal 'won' and the resulting outcome -- exactly what pure noise around a shared, roughly-stable baseline would look like.

reflection_shard.py's generative reflection loop (the actual TEXT that shadow_model.propose_from_reflection() keyword-scans) was directly confirmed to describe self-observation/free-association, not self-edit outcomes -- it has zero access to verification/quality data. The 'reflection' feeding Signal B is not outcome-grounded introspection in any meaningful sense.

The n~99,027 RiverBrain coding-bucket size could create an illusion of robustness: a large sample size makes the AVERAGE quality score itself well-estimated (2.37 is a precise number), but this investigation's own outcome-delta analysis (a DIFFERENT measurement, n=103, of whether a specific deploy event changed things) shows the actual causal intervention -- deploying a new self_edit_generated.py -- has a weak, statistically marginal, possibly-zero real effect on subsequent quality, regardless of how precisely the pre-deploy baseline is known.

The loop is real but demonstrably operates ONLY at the level of target selection (which task type gets attempted next), not at the level of response content or verified functional improvement -- consistent with, not contradicting, this investigation's own central finding.

final_classification.not_level_4_reason: No statistically defensible evidence of measurable iterative improvement was found. The 103 real, quality-tracked outcomes show a mean delta (+0.103) not distinguishable from zero at conventional significance (t=1.65, p~0.10), 40.8% of tracked deploys actively worsened quality, and mean delta shows no relationship to which targeting signal 'won' at decision time. Per this mission's own explicit rule, Level 4 is not awarded without direct outcome evidence, and the direct evidence gathered here argues against it, not merely fails to support it.
final_classification.why_level_3_and_not_lower: The feedback→self-model→targeting chain is real (not merely recorded, Level 1), demonstrably affects an actual downstream decision (target_task_type, real single instance observed causing a real deviation), and that decision is genuinely persistent across restart (self_model.json/shadow_self_model.json are both plain disk files re-read fresh each cycle, independently confirmed via this and the prior investigation's own restart-survival testing methodology). This is explicitly targeting-level, not content-level, adaptation, consistent with Hard Rule 6/7.

explicit_non_claims: This investigation does not establish why council_rater.py's polling stopped meaningfully advancing specifically around 2026-07-26 -- only that it did, and that a separate, later, confirmed rotation event (Aug 22) compounds the resulting staleness. The original trigger could not be recovered from currently-available logs.

This investigation cannot compute P(quality improvement | feedback-informed target) vs P(quality improvement | baseline target) as the mission's Part VIII requested, because 100% of the 103 real tracked outcomes share the same actual target -- there is no real historical contrast to condition on with this data.

This investigation does not establish that repairing the council-cursor bug would produce any measurable quality benefit -- only that it is structurally ready to and would flow through an already-verified blend mechanism.
This investigation does not resolve whether self_edit_convergence.json's zero-streak state reflects the failure-adjustment mechanism working correctly or being quietly inert.

This investigation does not establish that RiverBrain's coding-task-type dominance (99,027 observations) reflects a genuinely well-calibrated targeting choice versus a self-reinforcing artifact of coding simply being the most-sampled task type by construction (self-edit itself only ever generates code, mechanically feeding this bucket far more than personal/creative/reasoning could ever be fed by the same process).

This investigation does not claim the self-edit loop's real, Level-3 targeting adaptation constitutes learning, self-improvement, or content-level change of any kind -- per Hard Rules 6/7/9/10, it is reported strictly as persistent targeting adaptation.
